findings.reason: as written the unit-ownership is ambiguous (raw spelling vs `source_unit`), and the runtime table may be redundant if the census resolves the unit at authoring.
findings.text: §5 says the EDDB spelling is "turned into the unit string a binding declares as its `source_unit`", yet also says "an EDDB spelling with no entry is refused when the catalogue loads". The binding's `source_unit` is the DD unit (`imas_ambix/data/signal_map.py:89`), so a load-time refusal keyed on the EDDB spelling requires the binding to carry the raw string as well — the plan does not say it does, nor whether the mapping is stored so it can be consulted at load rather than resolved once at census time

findings.reason: the section adds a public definition while stating only that the existing names are kept, so the exported surface it creates cannot be reviewed.
findings.text: §6 generalises the equilibrium-convention entry point to take an equilibrium record through a loader with DIII-D, SELENE and FAME as loaders, but keeps `measure_diiid_convention` as the DIII-D entry (`imas_ambix/challenge/convention.py:266`); the generic entry the SELENE/FAME loaders call is never named and is not accounted for as public surface

interface_budget-1.reason: Acted in plan v114: section 6 names measure_convention(records, eligibility, *, shots) as one new public definition; measure_diiid_convention calls it.

thin_wrapper-1.reason: Acted in plan v114: section 5 resolves the EDDB spelling table at authoring; source_unit holds the DD unit and a test checks each binding against the table.

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the new modules that carry behaviour are deep: `imas_ambix/data/selene_deck.py` hides the `EQSLE.DATA`/`geo.in`/`coil_vv` grammars behind one converter. `imas_ambix/data/eddb_remote.py` hides transport, batch framing and the refusal protocol behind `RemoteEddbExtractor`; `imas_ambix/data/tokamap_export.py` hides the group/partition/key derivation behind one `export_tokamap_directory`. The catalogue/store additions are schema slots and one widened protocol argument, not a spread of wrappers.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: pass — I looked for forked placement, path resolution and state readers and found the plan extending the named owners rather than adding parallels: `machine_identity.default_registry` (keyed by machine, not a second registry), `gs/artifact_resolution.py` (`resolve_machine_description`/`author_pinned_description` take a machine), `data/eddb.py` (grid writer under the same store, not a second store over `JT60SA_ROOT`), `data/description_identity.py` (extended to the JT-60SA phases), and `spine_bench/shots.py` `resolve_shotset_version` (label widened, not a second labeller). `find imas_ambix -iname '*unit*'` and a grep for any `eqdb` symbol both return nothing, so the §5 table and the §7 EQDB reader are genuinely new rather than rebuilds.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — the current week's figures are public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; §6 generalises the convention scorer and keeps `measure_diiid_convention` exported but never names the generic entry the SELENE/FAME loaders call, so a new public definition is added without naming it or what it retires.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the plan names an existing owner for nearly every mechanism it touches and I opened each one; the owners exist and match the plan's account (see below), and the two codebases it names for discovery were searched by explicit census/sensor/geometry investigations recorded in its own sections.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — §5 adds a packaged EDDB-spelling→DD-unit table beside the binding's own declared `source_unit` and does not say which of the two owns the channel's unit.
